desc:
Each element of points is a distinct point [x, y]. Count the axis-aligned rectangles of positive area whose four corners are all points of the array. The sides of every such rectangle are parallel to the axes.

Each rectangle is counted once.

points = [[0,0],[0,1],[1,0],[1,1],[2,0],[2,1]]
rectangles: x in {0,1} with y in {0,1}; x in {0,2} with y in {0,1}; x in {1,2} with y in {0,1}
result = 3
hints: A rectangle is fixed by its bottom-left and top-right corners. Those two corners determine the other two.
Take every pair of points where one is strictly lower-left of the other. The rectangle is valid exactly when the other two corners, top-left and bottom-right, are also in the set.
Sort the points so each pair is visited once, and use a hash set for the membership tests.
editorial: Any axis-aligned rectangle has a unique bottom-left corner (x1, y1) and top-right corner (x2, y2) with x1 < x2 and y1 < y2. Its other corners are (x1, y2) and (x2, y1). So each rectangle is found by exactly one such diagonal pair.

Put the points in a set and sort them. For each pair i < j in sorted order, the second point has the larger x or the same x with a larger y. Keep the pairs with x2 > x1 and y2 > y1, then check the two remaining corners in the set.

With n points there are O(n<sup>2</sup>) pairs and each check is a constant-time set lookup, which is fast enough for n up to 600. Counting per column pair would be faster for dense inputs, but it is not needed here.
